name: Darier Disease

criteria.description: Presence of greasy, crusted, hyperkeratotic papules primarily in seborrheic areas
Histological evidence of suprabasal acantholysis and dyskeratosis with corps ronds and grains
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Characteristic nail abnormalities including V-shaped notching and longitudinal ridging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical papules in seborrheic areas plus histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ATP2A2 mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Greasy, crusted, hyperkeratotic papules in seborrheic areas
Nail abnormalities including V-shaped notching and longitudinal ridging
Histological suprabasal acantholysis with dyskeratosis (corps ronds and grains)

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial or fungal skin infections

occasional.notes: Reported in some patients, possibly related to disease burden

occasional.symptomName: Hair abnormalities such as fragility and brittleness

rare.symptomName: Erosions and ulcerations in severe disease

rare.notes: Rarely reported in association with Darier disease

laboratory: Histopathology showing suprabasal acantholysis with dyskeratotic cells (corps ronds and grains)
genetic: Mutations in ATP2A2 gene encoding SERCA2 calcium pump
other: Characteristic nail changes (V-shaped notching, longitudinal ridging)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows suprabasal acantholysis without dyskeratosis

redFlags: Rapid progression of erosive or ulcerative skin lesions
Secondary bacterial or fungal infections causing systemic symptoms
Neuropsychiatric symptoms including seizures or severe mood disorders
references: Burge SM. Darier-White disease: clinical features and management. Clin Exp Dermatol. 1994.
Boyden LM, et al. Mutations in ATP2A2, encoding a Ca2+ pump, cause Darier disease. Nat Genet. 2001.
